content.title: US Stock Market Hours 2026: Trading Times & Holiday Calendar
content.text: The US stock market is the largest capital market in the world, comprising the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE), NASDAQ, and the American Stock Exchange (AMEX). With daily trading volume exceeding $500 billion, it attracts investors from every corner of the globe. This guide covers US stock market trading hours for 2026, including regular sessions, pre-market and after-hours trading, daylight saving time adjustments, overnight trading developments, and the full holiday calendar. Regular Trading Hours The three major US exchanges share the same regular trading hours: 9:30 AM to 4:00 PM Eastern Time (ET), Monday through Friday. This 6.5-hour window is when liquidity and volume are at their peak, and the vast majority of institutional and retail trades are executed. Unlike some global markets, US exchanges do not close for a lunch break. Trading is continuous from open to close. Time Zone Conversions SessionEastern Time (ET)UTCLondon (GMT/BST)Tokyo (JST)Regular (Summer/DST)09:30 – 16:0013:30 – 20:0014:30 – 21:0022:30 – 05:00+1Regular (Winter/EST)09:30 – 16:0014:30 – 21:0014:30 – 21:0023:30 – 06:00+1 Daylight Saving Time The US observes Daylight Saving Time (DST), which shifts clocks forward by one hour in spring and back in autumn. For international investors, this means the market opens one hour earlier in their local time during DST. DST begins: Second Sunday in March (March 8, 2026) DST ends: First Sunday in November (November 1, 2026) US trading hours remain the same (9:30 AM – 4:00 PM ET) year-round. The change only affects the UTC offset (ET = UTC-4 during DST, UTC-5 during EST). Pre-Market Trading Pre-market trading runs from 4:00 AM to 9:30 AM ET. This extended session allows traders to react to overnight news, earnings releases, and economic data before the regular session opens. Key Characteristics Lower liquidity: Fewer participants mean wider bid-ask spreads Higher volatility: Earnings announcements and news events can cause sharp price movements Limit orders recommended: Market orders may execute at unfavorable prices due to thin order books Not universally available: Check with your broker whether pre-market access is offered Pre-market trading is commonly used for positioning ahead of anticipated market-moving events. The final hour before the regular open (8:30–9:30 AM ET) tends to see the highest pre-market activity, as key economic data is often released at 8:30 AM ET. After-Hours Trading After-hours trading runs from 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM ET. It shares similar characteristics with pre-market trading: lower liquidity, wider spreads, and potentially higher volatility. Common Use Cases Reacting to post-close earnings releases Adjusting overnight positions based on breaking news Managing risk ahead of the next trading day After-hours volume is typically 5–10% of the regular session. Large orders may not fill completely, and price discovery can be less reliable. Overnight Trading and the Move Toward 24-Hour Markets US exchanges are gradually extending trading hours. NYSE Arca has announced plans to expand to 22 hours per day (1:30 AM – 11:30 PM ET), which would cover the active trading hours of Asian and European markets. Several brokers, including Interactive Brokers and Robinhood, already offer extended overnight trading on select securities. This trend is driven by growing international demand for access to US equities outside of traditional hours. While true 24-hour trading has not yet been fully implemented, the direction is clear. Keep an eye on exchange announcements for updates. 2026 US Stock Market Holiday Calendar US markets are closed on all federal holidays and may close early (1:00 PM ET) on certain days preceding major holidays. 2026 Full-Day Closures DateHolidayJan 1 (Thu)New Year's DayJan 19 (Mon)Martin Luther King Jr. DayFeb 16 (Mon)Presidents' DayApr 3 (Fri)Good FridayMay 25 (Mon)Memorial DayJun 19 (Fri)JuneteenthJul 3 (Fri)Independence Day (observed)Sep 7 (Mon)Labor DayNov 26 (Thu)Thanksgiving DayDec 25 (Fri)Christmas Day 2026 Early Closures (1:00 PM ET) DateReasonNov 27 (Fri)Day after ThanksgivingDec 24 (Thu)Christmas Eve If a holiday falls on Saturday, markets typically close on the preceding Friday. If it falls on Sunday, markets close on the following Monday. Practical Tips for International Investors Focus on the Opening Hour The first hour of regular trading (9:30–10:30 AM ET) typically sees the highest volatility and volume of the entire session. If your schedule limits how much time you can dedicate to the US market, this is the most productive window. Use Conditional Orders For investors in Asia or Europe, the US market close falls in the early morning hours. Rather than staying up all night, set limit orders, stop-loss orders, and OCO (one-cancels-other) orders to automate your entry and exit points. Track Economic Data Releases Major US economic indicators, such as the Federal Reserve interest rate decision, Non-Farm Payrolls, and CPI, are typically released at 8:30 AM or 2:00 PM ET. Use an economic calendar to plan around these events. Mind the DST Switch Every March and November, the DST transition shifts market opening times by one hour for international investors. Update your trading alerts and schedules during the transition week. Frequently Asked Questions What are the US stock market trading hours? Regular trading hours are 9:30 AM to 4:00 PM Eastern Time, Monday through Friday. Pre-market trading begins at 4:00 AM ET, and after-hours trading continues until 8:00 PM ET. Does the US stock market close for lunch? No. Unlike the Tokyo Stock Exchange or Hong Kong Stock Exchange, US markets trade continuously from open to close without a midday break. When does Daylight Saving Time change in 2026? DST begins on March 8, 2026, and ends on November 1, 2026. During DST, the Eastern Time zone is UTC-4 instead of UTC-5. Is pre-market and after-hours trading risky? Extended-hours trading carries higher risk due to lower liquidity, wider spreads, and greater price volatility. Limit orders are strongly recommended over market orders in these sessions. How many holidays does the US stock market have in 2026? There are 10 full-day closures and 2 early-close days in 2026. The full calendar is listed above. Will the US stock market eventually trade 24 hours? NYSE Arca has announced plans to extend trading to 22 hours per day. Several brokers already offer limited overnight trading. Full 24-hour trading is expected to develop gradually over the coming years. Summary Understanding US stock market hours is essential for any investor participating in the world's largest equity market. Whether you trade during regular hours, take advantage of pre-market and after-hours sessions, or are preparing for the upcoming expansion to near-24-hour trading, knowing the schedule and its nuances gives you a meaningful edge. Use the time zone conversion tables and 2026 holiday calendar in this guide to plan your trading strategy. Combine conditional orders with an economic calendar to make the most of your available time.
